draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Munnar! You're about 1,600 metres up in the Western Ghats, in an old plantation town that still runs on tea. It usually has the most pleasant temperatures in all of Kerala.
draft.hungryLine: Munnar is a tea town first, so start with a cup grown on the slopes around you, then ask around town for a meal.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Mount Carmel Basilica is a 2 min walk, then the KDHP Tea Museum is about 2 km out to see how tea is processed. Save a morning for Eravikulam to meet the Nilgiri tahr.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head to Signal Point and look out over the Munnar Valley, with Chokarmudy and Anamudy hills in view. It's a properly relaxing spot.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Anamudi, inside Eravikulam National Park, is 2,695 m, the highest peak south of the Himalayas.

spots.name: Mount Carmel Basilica
spots.detail: 2 min walk · Wood-framed windows and a statue of Christ and the Virgin Mary

spots.name: KDHP Tea Museum
spots.detail: About 2 km away · A film, then a walk through the tea factory

spots.name: Eravikulam (Rajamalai) National Park
spots.detail: 45 min away · Home of the Nilgiri tahr

status.text: Closed around Feb to Mar for tahr breeding

legends.title: Why it's called Cigarette Point
legends.body: Back in the early plantation days, junior managers used to gather at this viewpoint to smoke. The nickname stuck, and people still call it Cigarette Point.

legends.title: Friendship calls
legends.body: Shout from one spot on the lake embankment and the hills send it back to you many times over. Young visitors come here just to call out to their friends and hear it echo.

tips.title: Reach Eravikulam before 8:30AM.
tips.body: After that the ticket queue can take a couple of hours, and the whole visit can run 4-5 hours.

tips.title: Pick a pedal boat at Kundala.
tips.body: Unless you really know how to row, a pedal boat is the easier way around the lake.

story.title: The first people
story.body: Around Marayoor, about 40 km away, there are natural caves with murals and relics from a late Stone Age civilisation. It's also the only place in Kerala where sandalwood grows naturally.

story.title: Training warriors
story.body: Kalarippayattu, the martial art you can watch in town, was used to train soldiers even before the Common Era. Today it's performed alongside Kathakali.

story.title: A tea town
story.body: Munnar grew as a plantation settlement dominated by tea. Old bungalows and cottages at Chithirapuram, about 10 km away, still carry that old world charm.

story.title: Swiss cows in the hills
story.body: Tamil migrant labourers once reared cattle at Mattupetty, and the cool climate made it ideal for the Indo-Swiss dairy farm, set up in 1961. It now rears more than 100 varieties of high-yielding cattle.

story.title: Hill station
story.body: Munnar is now a growing modern hill station and a favourite with Indian honeymooners. Tell me if you spot a tahr.
